chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Scoops Carey: saxophonist turned Chicago lawyer
summary: Collins came up with Carey, who joined Tatum's sextet at the same time, played with Earl Hines, then became a lawyer and died of cancer.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Had tremendous technique, very big sound. He was with Earl Hines, he did some very good things. He was with Earl Hines for quite a while. But we played around Chicago, we had a band around -- we had a little band around Chicago, and we joined Art Tatum at the same time. The Scoops was like a virtuoso on the saxophone. Scoops Carey, I'm surprised you haven't heard of him. But he died -- he -- a couple of years ago. I went back to his funeral, and he had gone into law, and he was a very big lawyer in Chicago. But "Jelly Jelly" -- he had a saxophone solo on "Jelly Jelly", and he did some very great things while he was with Earl and before even.
Art Tatum loved him.
